bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly Pay to Annual Salary

When you're comparing job offers or planning your finances, understanding how your hourly rate translates into annual pay is essential. At hourlytoannual.au, we help you convert your hourly wage to a yearly figure using the standard 38-hour week. This article explains the formula, the role of the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, tax, and superannuation—all while keeping the concept of **seek salary** in mind.

### The Standard Formula: Hourly × Hours per Week × 52

Annual gross pay is calculated by multiplying your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For full-time employees, the typical week is 38 ordinary hours. For example, if your hourly rate is $30, your annual salary would be $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. This assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

If you're paid fortnightly, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. Using the same example, weekly pay is $30 × 38 = $1,140, so fortnightly pay is $2,280. This can help you budget between pay cycles.

### National Minimum Wage vs. Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the base rate for award/agreement-free adult employees. However, most employees are covered by an award, which often sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for each award. Always check your award to ensure you're being paid correctly.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum rate, bringing the casual National Minimum Wage to $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave. When using our [timesheet](/), you can check a box to add casual loading to your base hourly rate—never enter a rate that already includes loading.

### Understanding Seek Salary in Context

When you search for jobs, you'll often see a **seek salary** range. This figure may be expressed as an annual package or an hourly rate. To compare offers accurately, convert everything to a common basis. For example, a job advertising $70,000 per year equates to roughly $35.45 per hour ($70,000 ÷ 38 ÷ 52). Conversely, an hourly rate of $40 gives an annual salary of $79,040. Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool helps with this.

Be aware that **seek salary** listings may include superannuation or not. In Australia, the super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your base salary. The Australian Taxation Office requires employers to pay super on top of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Always confirm whether the advertised salary is base salary or total package.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The 2026–27 resident tax rates are: nil on the first $18,200; 15% on the next $45,000; 30% on the next $135,000; 37% on the next $190,000; and 45% on anything above. Medicare levy is 2% (using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds are unconfirmed). Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator estimates net pay after tax and Medicare.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Super is calculated at 12% of your ordinary earnings, not deducted from your salary. For example, if your annual salary is $80,000, your employer must contribute $9,600 to your super fund, up to the $270,830 cap. This is separate from your take-home pay. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Using Our Reference Tables and Pay Guides

Our [reference tables](/data) provide the latest National Minimum Wage, award rates, and ABS Average Weekly Earnings. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, full-time adult ordinary time earnings averaged $2,083.70 per week in May 2026, while all employees (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week. These figures help you benchmark your **seek salary** against market rates.

### Final Tips

- Always use 38 hours per week unless your award specifies otherwise.
- Casual loading is 25% on top of the base rate.
- Super is 12% on top, not deducted.
- Tax and Medicare are estimates; use our [timesheet](/) for a personalised calculation.
- Check your award's pay guide from the Fair Work Ombudsman to ensure you're paid correctly.

By understanding these components, you can confidently evaluate any job offer and understand what your **seek salary** truly means for your annual earnings.
